what: The photo is carved with an 8×8 Bayer threshold in 3px cells and printed as dots in two colors, background and text (brightness gamma 1.7, two levels). A noise field (2.5×, .08 per second) shakes brightness by ±.12 so the dots shimmer slowly, and when the panel enters the 20~80% band of the screen it spreads from the center square outward in 1.6s power2.out. Dots on the same side as the page background are removed so the background shows through — when the section background changes, the removed side changes too. With look: hover it prints at 2px, four levels, threshold jitter .6 (redrawn per cell every 2 seconds), and when a hand is placed over it the original photo is revealed in Bayer order in .6s power2.out. active: <Selector> When it falls inside that selector (slide center), the original photo is revealed

options.look: base (default — 3px two-level dots, background removed) or hover (2px four-level dots, original photo on hover)
options.levels: Number of brightness steps, default 2 · hover 4
options.drift: Brightness range shaken by noise, default .12 · hover 0
options.knock: Subtract point — auto (picks by brightness of the backdrop, default) · dark · light · none
options.reveal: If off, fully expanded from the start
options.active: Original photo when inside this selector (e.g. .is-center)
options.--fx-dark: Dark dot color (css variable), default var(--kf-bg)
options.--fx-light: Bright dot color (css variable), default var(--kf-ink)

from.where: index.html .nc-layer .asset (sphere and shape render stipple) · recruit.html .nc-life .shot (look: hover) · .nc-gallery slide (active: .is-center) — original 3px · two levels · gamma 1.7 · noise .12 · spread 1.6s power2.out / hover 2px · four levels · .6s

note: Dots are drawn in CSS 1px units (device pixel ratio ignored) — cells must be crisp, so image-rendering: pixelated. The original draws a plate per photo on a single fixed canvas, while this part draws each photo with one WebGL context and then copies it to its own 2D canvas. Photos must be same-origin (or a data: URL) to be read as textures
